findings.text: the repair arm still omits tests/test_crew_watch_ensure.py and tests/test_watcher_arming_fallback.py although both import reckon.crew.runs and call ensure_watcher_service, so the done-when's importing-file measure covers 5 of the 7 callers of the changed function. This review ran both at the reviewed head (11 passed, EXIT=0), so nothing is red, but the node's own recorded evidence does not cover them.

there is no lock-table reader at this revision, but reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:lock_holders_in now owns the same /proc/locks FLOCK parse for a (device major, minor, inode) and landed on main in a parallel commit after this head, so the two readers should be consolidated onto that owner when the revisions meet.

_seat_is_held opens the watch lock and probes it with fcntl.flock, repeating the seat-held probe _register_watch_unit already performs in this module. The probe is small, and the lock paths are still correct, but the seat question is left without a single owner through which both callers read the kernel answer.

sent[0] == (999999, 15) compares the pid and signal the test itself handed in against what the monkeypatched signaller recorded, so the assertion cannot fail for a wrong pid or a wrong signal, and because the signaller is faked it can fail only when the code stops routing through the crew signaller, not when the signal that signaller raises is wrong. Durable because the seat cases prove pid selection against real processes, but it is a routing check.

sent_signals == ["SIGTERM"] holds the pid 999999 absent from the host's process table, but kernel pid_max is 4194304 here, so on a busy host a live 999999 makes the stop loop escalate to a faked SIGKILL and turns the case red for a reason unrelated to the routing it guards.

the node's gate file lies outside every declared write path: the dispatch names watch_unit.py and runs.py, the repair round adds the evidence fragment, the figures directory and tests/test_watch_seat_across_hosts.py, and none names this file, so promotion needs it ratified as an accepted path.
